title: Symmetry of the set disjointness function
statement: For every $n \in \bbn$ and all subsets $X, Y \subseteq [n]$, the disjointness function is symmetric in its two arguments: $\mathrm{disjointness}(n, X, Y) = \mathrm{disjointness}(n, Y, X)$. That is, since $X$ and $Y$ are disjoint if and only if $Y$ and $X$ are disjoint, swapping the two sets leaves the Boolean value unchanged.
replaced:
The disjointness function is symmetric in its two set arguments: for all
$X, Y \subseteq [n]$, $\mathrm{disjointness}(n, X, Y) = \mathrm{disjointness}(n, Y, X)$.
